From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-01-13T09:22:00-08:00
Subject: INTERNAL: NovumAI sizing draft (options + notes)

Irene / Marissa — initial sizing notes for NovumAI. I ran through three configurations; assumptions below and reasoning. Quotes inline are for the runbook we can hand to procurement.

Assumptions:
- Model baseline: llamaX-65B weights ~130GB (fp16).
- KV cache per token: per-layer KV doubles storage relative to single-token embedding; with 32 layers, rough incremental KV size ~= 48 bytes * context_length * layers / (1024^3) => ~0.048 GB per 100k tokens per 32-layer model (conservative estimate for planning). For 1M tokens this maps to ~0.48 GB * 10 = ~4.8 GB — but that number is per-layer-per-key; extra buffer, attention maps, and optimizer states push this higher. To be conservative we budget KV ~48GB for 1M tokens for llamaX-65B when accounting for layer replication and TP.
- Quantization factors: 8-bit -> ~2x reduction vs fp16; 4-bit -> ~3.5–4x reduction vs fp16 (effective model-weight sizes). Real-world kernels and padding reduce gains slightly.

Option A — Conservative (no quant, single-node multi-GPU):
- Model: llamaX-65B fp16 (weights ~130GB) + KV for 1M tokens ~48GB => total ~178GB
- Suggested hardware: 3 x 80GB A100 (NVLink) using model sharding (tensor parallel across 3 GPUs) + extra RNM for KV on GPU DRAM via NVLink.
- Pros: max fidelity, simplest debugging.
- Cons: high OPEX and larger reserved pool.

Option B — Balanced (8-bit quant + KV optimizations):
- Model: weights -> ~65GB after 8-bit quant (2x reduction), KV ~48GB => total ~113GB
- Suggested hardware: 2 x 80GB A100/H100 (NVLink) with an extra 80GB GPU for headroom (recommend reserve 3 GPUs per replica to maintain steady RPS and headroom for batch/prefill).
- Pros: 30–40% cost savings vs Option A, acceptable quality in most evals.
- Cons: limited headroom for 1M-context edge cases; may need fallback.

Option C — Aggressive (4-bit quant + sharded NVLink/multi-node):
- Model: weights -> ~35–40GB after 4-bit quant, KV ~48GB => total ~83–88GB
- Suggested hardware: 2 x 80GB H100 with NVLink + model parallelism (one replica can fit model + KV across 2 GPUs), or single 80GB with additional host-managed KV offload (PCIe) but that hits latency.
- Pros: lowest per-replica memory; best cost per token when quality acceptable.
- Cons: more complex kernels, higher risk of ML-quality regressions; some ops require fallback to fp16 for numeric stability.

Throughput sizing (steady 8 RPS, p95 700ms):
- Assume each replica (Option B) can sustain ~6–8 RPS at p95 for typical short generations (50–100 tokens). Pilot should provision 3 replicas for redundancy and autoscale burst to 6 replicas (covers spike to ~40 RPS if start/stop patterns align). For Option C, replicas can sustain slightly higher RPS but plan for canary testing before committing in prod.

Operational asks for NovumAI:
- NVLink across GPUs in each node (strongly recommended for 65B to avoid cross-node sharding latency).
- Support for sharded tensor parallel (TP) and model-parallel backends; plan for automatic fallback to 30B variant if memory/p95 targets violated.
- Reserve headroom for KV prefill during long-recall cold-starts. We recommend a burst pool (hot nodes) with additional GPUs for prefill-to-cache work.

I'll package these options into a short implementation runbook and attach numbers. Flag anything I missed.

-Karthik

Subject: Dedicated capacity recommendation + runbook for NovumAI (pilot -> prod)

Sam — attaching our capacity_runbook_v1.pdf and a short worksheet (novumai_requirements_sheet.xlsx). Summary and recommendation below.

Executive summary (pilot in 4 weeks):
- Pilot: 2x80GB H100 nodes (NVLink) per replica, start with Option B (8-bit quant + KV optimizations). Reserve 3 replicas (2 active + 1 standby) to meet steady 8 RPS and p95 targets; autoscale to 6 replicas for burst coverage.
- Production (12 weeks): move to reserved Dedicated pool of 12 x 80GB GPUs (3 replicas * baseline capacity * burst headroom) with a hot prefill pool of 2–3 GPUs to service KV cache population.
- Fallback policy: if evals show >1.5% quality drop at 8-bit on key prompts, fall back to 4-bit + mixed-fp16 kernels only for sensitive routes or to the 30B variant for latency-sensitive endpoints.

Why this mix: 8-bit gives the best balance of fidelity and immediate cost savings; 4-bit is attractive but requires canary/QA and some kernel work. For your 1M-token worst-cases we budgeted ~48GB for KV cache in sizing; this is conservative and includes layer replication and TP padding.

Attachments: capacity_runbook_v1.pdf (runbook with per-replica memory math), novumai_requirements_sheet.xlsx (please fill output-length column), draft_msa_novumai.pdf (for procurement).

Next steps:
- Sam: confirm output-length typical range and sign off on pilot hardware so we can provision Dedicated test nodes.
- Procurement: once signed MSA we will issue a Dedicated capacity sizing addendum with GPU SKU and reservation terms.

Thanks — looking forward to the pilot.
